Home / Evaluation

How scores work

Every resource is scored out of 100 by an automated evaluation (rubric v4.1). 61 of 62 resources are evaluated; the average score is 38.5.

Criteria

FAIR subtotal out of 48
CriterionMaxFormula
FFindable FAIR

F1 — the artefact has a persistent identifier: PURL, w3id or DOI (4). F4 — it is indexed in searchable services; counted across OLS, TIB, BioPortal, OBO Foundry, Bioregistry, FAIRsharing and LOV: ≥ 4 → 5, 3 → 4, 2 → 3, 1 → 1. F2 — a citable reference publication with a DOI (3).

124·[persistent identifier] + r(registries) + 3·[citable reference]
AAccessible FAIR

A1 — the machine-readable artefact (download PURL or repository) is retrievable over HTTP(S) (6) and the homepage resolves (3). A2 — metadata stays available even if the resource disappears, because it has a persistent record in a registry: OLS, TIB, BioPortal, OBO Foundry, Bioregistry, FAIRsharing or LOV (3). Hosts that refuse automated checks count as reachable.

123·[homepage reachable] + 6·[artefact retrievable over HTTP(S)] + 3·[metadata persists in a registry]
IInteroperable FAIR

I1 — a formal, broadly applicable language (OWL, OBO, Turtle, RDF, JSON-LD, LinkML, JSON Schema, SHACL, YAML schema, XSD) (5). I2 — a semantic-web representation (OWL, OBO, Turtle, RDF, JSON-LD, SHACL) whose terms are resolvable IRIs (3). I3 — qualified references to other vocabularies: ontologies it imports (OLS, Bioregistry, and owl:imports in the file itself) or whose terms it uses (at least 3 distinct terms in the file): ≥ 3 → 4, 1–2 → 2.

125·[formal format] + 3·[semantic-web IRIs] + i(imported vocabularies)
RReusable FAIR

R1.1 — a clear license: a recognised open license scores 5, any other stated license 2. R1.2 — provenance of releases: a version IRI or version info inside the artefact scores 4; a release tag or registry version only, 2. R1.3 — meets community standards: the better of the share of OBO Foundry principle checks passed on the OBO Dashboard (× 3) and a listing in FAIRsharing, a standards registry that reviews what it includes (2). LOV is counted under F4 and A2 only, so one listing isn't counted three times.

12license(5 open / 2 other) + version(4 in artefact / 2 elsewhere) + max(3·OBO principles pass rate, 2·[in FAIRsharing])
QOntology consistency & quality

Applies to ontologies (OWL/OBO/RDF artefacts). Logical consistency carries half the weight: a reasoner run (ROBOT + ELK, run by NeuroSchema on every ontology; the OBO Dashboard's result is used only if ours is missing) that finds the ontology consistent with no unsatisfiable classes scores 10; consistent with 1–5 unsatisfiable classes 5; more than 5 → 2; inconsistent, or the file could not be loaded, 0. OWL 2 DL profile 2. Upper-ontology alignment: imports or uses terms from BFO, COB, DOLCE, GFO or gUFO 3, the Relation Ontology 1 (read from the file as well as OLS and Bioregistry). Quality report: no ROBOT errors 2, warnings per class ≤ 0.05 → 1 (both only for OBO-style ontologies, since the ROBOT report checks OBO conventions), and a pitfall scan with no critical pitfalls 1. A check that could not be run (no retrievable artefact, file too large, tool timed out) is not assessed: its points are left out of the possible total, and the grade is flagged "Q partially assessed". Schemas, atlases and other non-ontology resources are not scored on Q; their total is scaled to 100 from the remaining 80 points.

20c(logical consistency) + 2·[OWL 2 DL] + u(upper ontology) + q(quality report)
MMaintenance

Recency of the latest commit, release or dated file: ≤ 3 months 10, ≤ 6 months 8, ≤ 1 year 5, ≤ 2 years 2, older 0. Release cadence — distinct releases in the last 12 months (GitHub releases, dated tags, version IRIs across runs): ≥ 6 → 6, ≥ 4 → 5, ≥ 2 → 3, 1 → 2.

16recency(months) + cadence(releases in last 12 months)
UCommunity adoption

Documented adopting projects (curated, OBO Foundry usages): ≥ 8 → 7, ≥ 5 → 5, ≥ 3 → 4, ≥ 1 → 2. Reuse — other ontologies that import it (OBO Dashboard, OLS, Bioregistry): ≥ 30 → 4, ≥ 10 → 3, ≥ 3 → 2, ≥ 1 → 1. Community signal, the better of GitHub stars (≥ 500 → 5, ≥ 100 → 4, ≥ 25 → 2, ≥ 5 → 1) and reference-paper citations (≥ 1000 → 5, ≥ 300 → 4, ≥ 50 → 2, ≥ 10 → 1).

16a(adopting projects) + reuse(ontologies importing it) + max(stars, citations)
PPenalties (inactivity & inconsistency)

Problems are marked down, not just left unrewarded. Inactivity: after a one-year grace period every further year without public activity deducts 4 points (up to 20); archived, legacy or OBO-inactive resources lose a further 10; with no activity evidence at all, 5. Consistency: a logically inconsistent ontology loses 20 and can score no higher than 54 (grade D). Critical pitfalls (OOPS!, e.g. cycles in the class hierarchy, multiple domains/ranges, ambiguous namespace) cost 3 per pitfall type, up to 12. Unsatisfiable classes and ROBOT report errors already cost Q points, so they are not penalised again here. The penalty is capped at 50 and the total never drops below 0.

—min(50, inactivity + 10·[archived/legacy/OBO-inactive] + 20·[inconsistent] + min(12, 3·critical pitfall types)). Inconsistent ontologies are capped at 54 (grade D).

Grades: A ≥ 85 · B ≥ 70 · C ≥ 55 · D ≥ 40 · E ≥ 0. Grade counts: A 7 · B 3 · C 6 · D 9 · E 36 · not evaluated 1.
